an6.41:1.2: that on one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Rājagaha on Vulture Peak Mountain.
an6.41:1.3: Then early in the morning, Ven. Sāriputta, having adjusted his lower robe and carrying his bowl & outer robe, was coming down from Vulture Peak Mountain with a large group of monks when he saw a large wood pile off to one side.
an6.41:1.4: Seeing it, he said to the monks,
an6.41:1.5: “Friends, do you see that large wood pile over there?”
an6.41:2.1: “Friends, if he wanted to, a monk with psychic power, having attained mastery of his mind, could will that wood pile to be nothing but earth.
an6.41:2.3: There is earth-property [or: earth-potential] in that wood pile, in dependence on which he could will that wood pile to be nothing but earth.
an6.41:2.4: “If he wanted to, a monk with psychic power, having attained mastery of his mind, could will that wood pile to be nothing but water…
an6.41:2.10: There is the property of the unattractive in that wood pile, in dependence on which he could will that wood pile to be nothing but unattractive.”
